title.zh: 卷一百九十二 列傳第七十九: 良吏二
title.raw: 卷一百九十二 列傳第七十九: 良吏二 Volume 192 Biographies 79: Virtuous Officials 2

sentences.zh: 耶律伯堅，字壽之，桓州人。

translations.literal: Yelü Bojian, style name Shouzhi, was a man of Huanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yelü Bojian, whose courtesy name was Shouzhi, came from Huanzhou.

sentences.zh: 氣豪俠，喜與名士遊。

translations.literal: His spirit was bold and chivalrous; he delighted in traveling with eminent scholars.
translations.idiomatic: He was spirited and chivalrous, and loved to keep company with men of renown.

sentences.zh: 用薦舉入官，為工部主事。

translations.literal: Through recommendation he entered office and served as a clerk in the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended for office, he became a clerk in the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 至元九年，轉保定路清苑縣尹。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Zhiyuan he was transferred to be magistrate of Qingyuan County in Baoding Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In 1272 he was reassigned as magistrate of Qingyuan County on the Baoding circuit.

sentences.zh: 初，安肅州苦徐水之害，訴於大司農司，大司農司欲奪水故道，導水使東。

translations.literal: At first Ansu Prefecture suffered from the harm of the Xu River and appealed to the Grand Agricultural Commission; the commission wished to seize the river's old course and divert the water eastward.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Ansu Prefecture had long suffered flooding from the Xu River and petitioned the Grand Agricultural Commission, which proposed to seize the river's former channel and divert its waters east.

sentences.zh: 東則清苑境也，地勢不利，果導之，則清苑被其害，而水亦必反故道為災。

translations.literal: To the east was Qingyuan territory; the terrain was unfavorable. If the water were truly diverted, Qingyuan would suffer the harm, and the water would also inevitably return to its old course and become a disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Eastward lay Qingyuan's territory, where the lay of the land was unfavorable; if the diversion went ahead, Qingyuan would be harmed, and the river would surely revert to its old course and bring disaster again.

sentences.zh: 伯堅陳其形勢，圖其利害，要大司農司官及郡守行視可否，事遂得已。

translations.literal: Bojian set forth the terrain, charted the advantages and harms, and required officials of the Grand Agricultural Commission and the circuit intendant to go and inspect whether it was feasible; the matter was then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Bojian explained the terrain, mapped out the risks and benefits, and insisted that Grand Agricultural officials and the circuit intendant inspect the site in person; the plan was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 縣西有塘水，溉民田甚廣，勢家據以為磑，民以失利來訴。

translations.literal: West of the county was pond water that irrigated the people's fields over a very wide area; powerful families had seized it to make water mills, and the people came to sue over their lost benefit.
translations.idiomatic: West of the county stood a reservoir whose waters irrigated a vast stretch of farmland; powerful families had monopolized it for water mills, and the peasants sued over their lost irrigation.

sentences.zh: 伯堅命毀磑，決其水而注之田，許以溉田之餘月，乃得堰水置磑。

translations.literal: Bojian ordered the mills destroyed, released the water and poured it into the fields, and permitted mills only in the months left over from irrigation before one might dam the water and set up mills.
translations.idiomatic: Bojian ordered the mills torn down, released the water back into the fields, and allowed mills only in the off-season after irrigation—only then might the water be dammed for milling.

sentences.zh: 仍以其事聞於省部，著為定制。

translations.literal: He still reported the matter to the provincial offices, and it was written as a standing regulation.
translations.idiomatic: He also reported the case to the provincial administration, and it was enacted as a permanent rule.

sentences.zh: 縣居南北之衝，歲為親王大官治供帳於縣西，限以十月成，至明年復撤而新之，吏得併緣侵漁，其費不貲。

translations.literal: The county lay on the crossroads of north and south; each year for princes of the blood and high officials quarters and supplies were prepared west of the county, required to be finished by the tenth month; the next year they would be torn down and made new again; clerks could use every pretext to embezzle, and the expense was incalculable.
translations.idiomatic: The county sat on the main route between north and south; every year quarters and provisions for imperial princes and high officials were erected west of the town, due by the tenth month, then torn down and rebuilt the next year—giving clerks endless chances to skim funds until the cost was beyond reckoning.

sentences.zh: 伯堅命築公館，以代供帳，其弊遂絕。

translations.literal: Bojian ordered a public lodge built to replace the quarters and supplies, and that abuse was ended.
translations.idiomatic: Bojian had a public guesthouse built to replace the annual encampments, and the abuse ceased.

sentences.zh: 凡郡府賦役，於縣有重於他縣者，輒曰：「寧得罪於上，不可得罪於下。

translations.literal: Whenever prefectural levies and corvée bore more heavily on this county than on others, he would say: "Better to offend those above than to offend those below."
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the prefecture imposed levies or corvée heavier on his county than on others, he would say, "Better to anger my superiors than to wrong the people below."

sentences.zh: 」必詣府力爭之。

translations.literal: " He invariably went to the prefecture and strove against it with force.
translations.idiomatic: " He always went to the prefectural seat and fought the matter through.

sentences.zh: 在清苑四年，民親戴之如父母，比去而猶思之，立石頌其德焉。

translations.literal: During four years in Qingyuan the people cherished him as parents; when he left they still thought of him and erected a stone to praise his virtue.
translations.idiomatic: In four years at Qingyuan the people loved him as they would their own parents; long after he left they still missed him and set up a stone praising his virtue.

sentences.zh: 擢為恩州同知。

translations.literal: He was promoted to vice-prefect of En Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice-prefect of En Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 段直，字正卿，澤州晉城人。

translations.literal: Duan Zhi, style name Zhengqing, was a man of Jincheng in Ze Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Zhi, whose courtesy name was Zhengqing, came from Jincheng in Ze Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 至元十一年，河北、河東、山東盜賊充斥，直聚其鄉黨族屬，結壘自保。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Zhiyuan bandits filled Hebei, Hedong, and Shandong; Zhi gathered his townsmen and kinsmen, built fortifications, and protected themselves.
translations.idiomatic: In 1274, as bandits overran Hebei, Hedong, and Shandong, Zhi rallied his clansmen and neighbors, built a fortified camp, and held their ground.

sentences.zh: 世祖命大將略地晉城，直以其眾歸之，幕府承製，署直潞州元帥府右監軍。

translations.literal: The Founder ordered a great general to reduce Jincheng; Zhi brought his host to submit; the headquarters issued orders on authority and appointed Zhi Right Overseer of the Lu Prefecture Marshal's Office.
translations.idiomatic: Kublai sent a great general to take Jincheng; Zhi submitted with his followers, and the field command, acting on imperial warrant, appointed him Right Overseer of the Lu Prefecture Marshal's Office.

sentences.zh: 其後論功行賞，分土世守，命直佩金符，為澤州長官。

translations.literal: Afterward merits were assessed and rewards given; lands were divided for perpetual tenure; Zhi was ordered to wear a gold tally and made chief administrator of Ze Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when merits were rewarded with hereditary fiefs, he was ordered to wear a gold tally and made chief administrator of Ze Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 澤民多避兵未還者，直命籍其田廬於親戚鄰人之戶，且約曰：「俟業主至，當析而歸之。

translations.literal: Many people of Ze had fled the soldiers and not returned; Zhi ordered their fields and houses registered to the households of relatives and neighbors, and stipulated: "When the owners arrive, they shall be divided and returned."
translations.idiomatic: Many Ze residents had fled the fighting and not returned; Zhi had their fields and houses registered under relatives and neighbors, with the stipulation: "When the owners come back, everything will be divided and restored to them."

sentences.zh: 」逃民聞之，多來還者，命歸其田廬如約，民得安業。

translations.literal: " When fleeing people heard this, many came back; he ordered their fields and houses returned according to the agreement, and the people were able to settle in their occupations.
translations.idiomatic: " Refugees heard of this and many returned; he restored their property as promised, and the people could resume their livelihoods in peace.

sentences.zh: 素無產者，則出粟賑之；

translations.literal: Those who from the first had no property—he then issued grain to relieve them;
translations.idiomatic: Those who owned nothing received grain from his stores;

sentences.zh: 為他郡所俘掠者，出財購之；

translations.literal: those seized and plundered by other prefectures—he spent wealth to redeem them;
translations.idiomatic: those captured and carried off to other prefectures were ransomed at his expense;

sentences.zh: 以兵死而暴露者，收而瘞之。

translations.literal: those who died in war and lay exposed—he gathered and buried them.
translations.idiomatic: and the bodies of soldiers left unburied on the field he gathered in and interred.

sentences.zh: 未幾，澤為樂土。

translations.literal: Before long Ze became a land of peace and joy.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Ze had become a peaceful, thriving country.

sentences.zh: 大修孔子廟，割田千畝，置書萬卷，迎儒士李俊民為師，以招延四方來學者。

translations.literal: He greatly repaired the Temple of Confucius, cut off a thousand mu of fields, set up ten thousand scrolls of books, welcomed the scholar Li Junmin as teacher, and thereby drew in learners from the four quarters.
translations.idiomatic: He greatly restored the Temple of Confucius, endowed a thousand mu of land, assembled ten thousand volumes, and invited the scholar Li Junmin as master to attract students from far and wide.

sentences.zh: 不五六年，學之士子，以通經被選者，百二十有二人。

translations.literal: Within not five or six years, among the school's scholars those selected for mastering the classics numbered one hundred twenty-two.
translations.idiomatic: Within five or six years, one hundred twenty-two students versed in the classics had passed selection for office.

sentences.zh: 在官二十年，多有惠政。

translations.literal: In office twenty years he had many benevolent policies.
translations.idiomatic: During twenty years in office he enacted many policies that benefited the people.

sentences.zh: 朝廷特命提舉本州學校事，未拜而卒。

translations.literal: The court specially appointed him to supervise the prefectural schools, but before he took office he died.
translations.idiomatic: The court specially appointed him to oversee the prefectural schools, but he died before he could assume the post.

sentences.zh: 諳都剌，字瑞芝，凱烈氏。

translations.literal: Nadula, style name Ruizhi, of the Kailie clan.
translations.idiomatic: Nadula, whose courtesy name was Ruizhi, belonged to the Kailie clan.

sentences.zh: 祖阿思蘭，嘗從大將阿術伐宋，仕至冀寧路達魯花赤，子孫因其名蘭，遂以蘭為氏。

translations.literal: His grandfather Aslan had once followed the great general Aju in campaigning against Song, served up to darughachi of Jining Circuit, and descendants because of his name Lan took Lan as their surname.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Aslan had followed the great general Aju in the campaigns against Song and rose to darughachi of Jining Circuit; later generations took the syllable Lan from his name as their surname.

sentences.zh: 諳都剌通經史，兼習諸國語。

translations.literal: Nadula was versed in the classics and histories and also studied the various national languages.
translations.idiomatic: Nadula was learned in the classics and histories and fluent in several of the empire's languages.

sentences.zh: 成宗時，為翰林院札爾里赤，職書制誥。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Chengzong he was a jarligchi of the Hanlin Academy, with the duty of drafting edicts and patents.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Chengzong he served in the Hanlin Academy as jarligchi, drafting imperial edicts and patents.

sentences.zh: 會有旨命書籓王添力聖旨，諳都剌曰：「此旨非惟有虧國體，行且為民殃矣。

translations.literal: It happened that an order came to draft an edict for the feudatory prince Tianli; Nadula said: "This edict not only damages the dignity of the state—it will soon become a calamity for the people as well."
translations.idiomatic: When an order came to draft an edict for the feudatory prince Tianli, Nadula said, "This edict would not only compromise the dignity of the state—it would soon bring disaster on the people as well."

sentences.zh: 」帝聞之，謂近臣曰：「小吏如此，真難得也。

translations.literal: " When the emperor heard this he said to close attendants: "For a petty clerk to be like this is truly hard to come by."
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor heard of it and told his close attendants, "For a junior clerk to speak so is truly rare."

sentences.zh: 」事乃止。

translations.literal: " The matter was then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: " The matter was dropped.

sentences.zh: 尋授應奉翰林文字，凡蒙古傳記，多所校正。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Hanlin Attendant for Documents; for all Mongol biographies he made many corrections.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed Hanlin Attendant for Documents and corrected numerous errors in Mongol-language biographical records.

sentences.zh: 升待制。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Academician-in-Waiting.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Academician-in-Waiting.

sentences.zh: 時方選守令，除遼州達魯花赤，以最聞，賜上尊名幣，除集賢直學士。

translations.literal: At that time they were selecting prefects and magistrates; he was appointed darughachi of Liaozhou, became known for excellence, was granted fine wine and famous silks, and appointed Direct Scholar of the Hall of Gathered Talents.
translations.idiomatic: When the court was selecting local administrators, he was made darughachi of Liaozhou; renowned for outstanding service, he received imperial gifts of wine and silk and was appointed Direct Scholar of the Hall of Gathered Talents.

sentences.zh: 至順元年，遷襄陽路達魯花赤。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhishun he was transferred to darughachi of Xiangyang Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In 1330 he was transferred to darughachi of Xiangyang Circuit.

sentences.zh: 山西大饑，河南行省恐流民入境為變，檄守武關，諳都剌驗其良民，輒聽其度關。

translations.literal: Shanxi suffered great famine; the Henan Branch Secretariat feared that wandering people entering the border would cause disorder and issued orders to guard Wuguan Pass; Nadula examined those who were good commoners and always allowed them to cross the pass.
translations.idiomatic: When Shanxi was stricken by severe famine, the Henan Branch Secretariat, fearing unrest from refugees, ordered Wuguan Pass held; Nadula inspected those who were plainly honest folk and let them cross.

sentences.zh: 吏曰：「得無違上命乎？

translations.literal: A clerk said: "Will this not violate the superior's command?"
translations.idiomatic: A clerk asked, "Will this not defy your superiors' orders?"

sentences.zh: 」諳都剌曰：「吾防奸耳，非仇良民也，可不開其生路耶！

translations.literal: " Nadula said: "I guard against villains, not bear enmity toward good commoners—how can one not open a path of life for them!"
translations.idiomatic: " Nadula replied, "I am guarding against wrongdoers, not making enemies of honest people—should we not leave them a way to live?"

sentences.zh: 」既又煮粥以食之，所活數万人。

translations.literal: " He then also cooked porridge to feed them; those who lived numbered tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: " He also had porridge cooked to feed them, saving tens of thousands of lives.

sentences.zh: 又城臨漢水，歲有水患，為築堤城外，遂以無虞。

translations.literal: Moreover the city bordered the Han River and each year had water disasters; he built dikes outside the walls, and thereafter there was no worry.
translations.idiomatic: The city also stood on the Han River and suffered annual floods; he built dikes outside the walls, and the danger passed.

sentences.zh: 元統二年，除益都路總管。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yuantong he was appointed circuit intendant of Yidu.
translations.idiomatic: In 1334 he was appointed circuit intendant of Yidu.

sentences.zh: 俗頗悍黠，而諳都剌務興學校，以平易治之。

translations.literal: The customs were quite fierce and cunning, yet Nadula devoted himself to establishing schools and governed them with ease and fairness.
translations.idiomatic: The local customs were fierce and cunning, but Nadula devoted himself to schools and governed with a light, even hand.

sentences.zh: 有上馬賊白晝劫人，久不能捕，諳都剌生擒之，其黨賂宣慰使羅鍋，誣以枉勘，縱其賊。

translations.literal: There were mounted bandits who robbed people in broad daylight; for long they could not be captured; Nadula seized them alive; their gang bribed the pacification commissioner Luo Guo, falsely charged him with wrongful investigation, and released the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Mounted bandits had long robbed travelers by day without being caught; Nadula captured them alive, but their accomplices bribed Pacification Commissioner Luo Guo to accuse him of wrongful prosecution and secured the bandits' release.

sentences.zh: 已而賊劫河間，復被獲，乃盡輸其情，而諳都剌之誣始白，俾再任一考。

translations.literal: Before long the bandits raided Hejian, were captured again, and then fully confessed the facts; Nadula's false charge was first cleared, and he was permitted to serve another term of evaluation.
translations.idiomatic: Later the bandits struck Hejian, were captured again, and confessed everything; Nadula's innocence was finally established, and he was allowed to serve another term.

sentences.zh: 親王買奴鎮益都，其府屬病民，諳都剌裁抑之，民以無擾。

translations.literal: The imperial prince Mainu was stationed at Yidu; his household staff harmed the people; Nadula restrained and checked them, and the people were undisturbed.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Prince Mainu was stationed at Yidu, and his household staff preyed on the people; Nadula curbed them, and the populace was left in peace.

sentences.zh: 至正六年卒，年七十。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Zhizheng he died, aged seventy.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 1346 at the age of seventy.

sentences.zh: 子燮徹堅，同知新喻州事，以孝稱。

translations.literal: His son Xiechejian was vice-prefect of Xinyu Prefecture and was known for filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xiechejian served as vice-prefect of Xinyu Prefecture and was famed for his filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 楊景行，字賢可，吉安太和州人。

translations.literal: Yang Jingxing, style name Xiankai, was a man of Taihe Prefecture in Ji'an.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Jingxing, whose courtesy name was Xiankai, came from Taihe Prefecture in Ji'an.

sentences.zh: 登延祐二年進士第，授贛州路會昌州判官。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the second year of Yanyou and was appointed assistant prefect of Huichang Prefecture on the Ganzhou circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in 1315 and was appointed assistant prefect of Huichang on the Ganzhou circuit.

sentences.zh: 會昌民素不知井飲，汲於河流，故多疾癘；

translations.literal: The people of Huichang from of old did not know well-water drinking; they drew from the river, and therefore had many pestilences;
translations.idiomatic: The people of Huichang had never drawn drinking water from wells but took it from the river, and so suffered frequent epidemics;

sentences.zh: 不知陶瓦，以茅覆屋，故多火災。

translations.literal: they did not know pottery tiles and used thatch to cover houses, and therefore had many fires.
translations.idiomatic: nor did they know fired tiles and roofed their houses with thatch, which led to many fires.

sentences.zh: 景行教民穿井以飲，陶瓦以代茅茨，民始免於疾癘火災。

translations.literal: Jingxing taught the people to dig wells for drinking and to use pottery tiles in place of thatch; the people were then freed from pestilence and fire disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Jingxing taught them to sink wells for drinking water and to use tiles instead of thatch, and they were finally spared epidemics and conflagrations.

sentences.zh: 豪民十人，號十虎，干政害民，悉捕置之法。

translations.literal: Ten powerful commoners, called the Ten Tigers, meddled in government and harmed the people; he captured them all and applied the law.
translations.idiomatic: Ten powerful locals, known as the Ten Tigers, had meddled in government and preyed on the people; he arrested them all and punished them according to law.

sentences.zh: 乃創學舍，禮師儒，勸民斥腴田以膳士，弦誦之聲遂盛。

translations.literal: He then founded a school building, honored teacher-scholars, urged the people to set aside fertile fields to feed scholars, and the sound of chanting the classics then flourished.
translations.idiomatic: He founded a school, honored Confucian teachers, and urged the people to donate fertile land to support students; soon the sound of classical study filled the district.

sentences.zh: 調永新州判官，奉郡府命，核民田租，除剷宿弊，姦欺不容，細民賴焉。

translations.literal: Transferred to assistant prefect of Yongxin, he received the prefectural command, audited the people's field rents, removed long-standing abuses, allowed no crafty deception, and the lesser people relied on this.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to Yongxin as assistant prefect, he carried out the prefecture's order to audit land rents, uprooted entrenched abuses, tolerated no fraud, and the common people were the beneficiaries.

sentences.zh: 改江西行省照磨，轉撫州路宜黃縣尹，理白冤獄之不決者數十事。

translations.literal: He was changed to Records Examiner of the Jiangxi Branch Secretariat, then transferred to magistrate of Yihuang County on the Fuzhou circuit, and cleared dozens of unjust cases that had not been decided.
translations.idiomatic: He became Records Examiner of the Jiangxi Branch Secretariat, then magistrate of Yihuang County on the Fuzhou circuit, where he resolved dozens of long-stalled wrongful convictions.

sentences.zh: 升撫州路總管府推官，發擿姦伏，郡無冤獄。

translations.literal: Promoted to judicial investigator of the Fuzhou Circuit Intendant's office, he exposed hidden wrongdoing and the prefecture had no unjust prisons.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to judicial investigator of the Fuzhou circuit administration, he exposed hidden crimes until the circuit held no wrongful cases.

sentences.zh: 金溪縣民陶甲，厚積而凶險，嘗屢誣陷其縣長吏罷去之，由是官吏畏其人，不敢詰治，陶遂暴橫於一郡。

translations.literal: In Jinxi County the commoner Tao Jia had amassed great wealth and was fierce and treacherous; he had repeatedly framed and brought down the county's chief officials, and thereby officials feared the man and dared not investigate and punish; Tao then rampaged across the whole prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: At Jinxi County a man named Tao Jia had grown wealthy and vicious; he had repeatedly framed county magistrates until they were removed, so that officials feared him and dared not prosecute, and Tao tyrannized the entire prefecture.

sentences.zh: 景行至，以法痛繩之，徙五百里外。

translations.literal: When Jingxing arrived he punished him severely by law and exiled him five hundred li beyond.
translations.idiomatic: When Jingxing arrived he punished Tao severely under the law and exiled him five hundred li away.

sentences.zh: 金溪豪僧云住，發人塚墓取財物，事覺，官吏受賄，緩其獄，景行急按之，僧以賄動之，不聽，乃賂當道者，以危語撼之，一不顧，卒治之如法。

translations.literal: In Jinxi the powerful monk Yunzhu opened people's tombs and graves to take valuables; when the matter was discovered officials took bribes and slowed his case; Jingxing pressed the investigation urgently; the monk tried to move him with bribes—he would not listen—then bribed those in power and used threatening words to shake him; he paid no heed and finally punished him according to law.
translations.idiomatic: A powerful Jinxi monk named Yunzhu had robbed graves for valuables; when the crime came to light, officials took bribes and delayed the case. Jingxing pressed the investigation; the monk tried to bribe him, then bribed higher authorities and threatened him with ominous words, but Jingxing ignored it all and punished the monk by law.

sentences.zh: 由是豪猾屏跡，良民獲安。

translations.literal: From this the fierce and cunning withdrew from sight and good commoners obtained peace.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter the violent and cunning kept out of sight, and honest people lived in peace.

sentences.zh: 轉湖州路歸安縣尹，奉行省命，理荒田租，民無欺弊。

translations.literal: Transferred to magistrate of Gui'an County on the Huzhou circuit, he carried out the Branch Secretariat's order, settled rents on abandoned fields, and the people had no fraudulent abuses.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to magistrate of Gui'an on the Huzhou circuit, he carried out the secretariat's order to settle rents on abandoned fields, and the people were no longer cheated.

sentences.zh: 景行所歷州縣，皆有惠政；

translations.literal: In every prefecture and county Jingxing passed through he had benevolent policies;
translations.idiomatic: Every prefecture and county Jingxing served benefited from his policies;

sentences.zh: 所去，民皆立石頌之。

translations.literal: wherever he left, the people all erected stones to praise him.
translations.idiomatic: and wherever he left office the people erected stones in his praise.

sentences.zh: 以翰林待制、朝列大夫致仕，年七十四卒。

translations.literal: He retired with the titles Hanlin Academician-in-Waiting and Grand Master for Court Audience, and died at seventy-four.
translations.idiomatic: He retired with the ranks of Hanlin Academician-in-Waiting and Grand Master for Court Audience and died at seventy-four.

sentences.zh: 林興祖，字宗起，福州羅源人。

translations.literal: Lin Xingzu, style name Zongqi, was a man of Luoyuan in Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Lin Xingzu, whose courtesy name was Zongqi, came from Luoyuan in Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 至治二年，登進士第，授承事郎、同知黃岩州事，三遷而知鉛山州。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhizhi he passed the jinshi examination, was appointed Gentleman for Managing Affairs and vice-prefect of Huangyan, and after three promotions became prefect of Qianshan.
translations.idiomatic: In 1322 he passed the jinshi examination, was appointed Gentleman for Managing Affairs and vice-prefect of Huangyan, and after three promotions became prefect of Qianshan.

sentences.zh: 鉛山素多造偽鈔者，豪民吳友文為之魁，遠至江淮、燕薊，莫不行使。

translations.literal: Qianshan from of old had many makers of counterfeit notes; the powerful commoner Wu Youwen was their leader; as far as the Jiang-Huai and Yan-Ji regions, none did not circulate them.
translations.idiomatic: Qianshan had long been rife with counterfeiters of paper money; a powerful local named Wu Youwen led them, and their notes circulated as far as the Jiang-Huai region and the Yan-Ji capital area.

sentences.zh: 友文姦黠悍鷙，因偽造致富，乃分遣惡少四五十人，為吏於有司，伺有欲告之者，輒先事戕之，前後殺人甚眾，奪人妻女十一人為妾，民罹其害，銜冤不敢訴者十餘年。

translations.literal: Youwen was crafty, cunning, fierce, and brutal; through counterfeiting he grew rich, then sent out forty or fifty vicious youths to serve as clerks in the offices; when he spied anyone wishing to report him he would first kill them; before and after he killed very many people; he seized eleven men's wives and daughters as concubines; the people suffered his harm and bore grievances yet dared not sue for more than ten years.
translations.idiomatic: Youwen was cunning, ruthless, and violent; counterfeiting had made him rich, and he placed forty or fifty thugs as clerks in government offices to spy on accusers and kill them first—he murdered many over the years, seized eleven women as concubines, and for more than a decade the people suffered in silence, too afraid to bring suit.

sentences.zh: 興祖至官，曰：「此害不除，何以牧民！

translations.literal: When Xingzu reached office he said: "If this harm is not removed, how can one shepherd the people!"
translations.idiomatic: When Xingzu took office he said, "If this scourge is not removed, how can I govern the people?"

sentences.zh: 」即張榜禁偽造者，且立賞募民首告。

translations.literal: " He immediately posted notices forbidding counterfeiters and also set a reward to recruit the people to report first.
translations.idiomatic: " He immediately posted notices banning counterfeiting and offered rewards for informants.

sentences.zh: 俄有告者至，佯以不實斥去；

translations.literal: Soon a reporter came; he pretended to reject him as untrue and drove him away;
translations.idiomatic: Soon an informant came forward; Xingzu pretended to dismiss the charge as false and sent him away;

sentences.zh: 又有告獲偽造二人並贓者，乃鞫之，款成。

translations.literal: then another report came that two counterfeiters and the evidence had been seized; he then interrogated them and the confession was complete.
translations.idiomatic: then another report arrived that two counterfeiters had been caught with the evidence; he interrogated them until they confessed fully.

sentences.zh: 友文自至官，為之營救，興祖命並執之。

translations.literal: Youwen himself came to the office to work for their rescue; Xingzu ordered him seized as well.
translations.idiomatic: Youwen came in person to lobby for their release; Xingzu ordered him arrested too.

sentences.zh: 須臾，來訴友文者百餘人，擇其重罪一二事鞫之，獄立具，逮捕其黨二百餘人，悉置之法。

translations.literal: In a moment more than a hundred came to sue Youwen; he selected one or two of the grave crimes and interrogated them; the case was immediately complete; he arrested his gang of more than two hundred and all were punished by law.
translations.idiomatic: Within moments more than a hundred people came forward to accuse Youwen; Xingzu chose one or two of the gravest charges, secured a swift conviction, arrested more than two hundred accomplices, and punished them all by law.

sentences.zh: 民害既去，政聲籍甚。

translations.literal: Once the people's harm was removed, his governmental reputation was greatly renowned.
translations.idiomatic: With the people's scourge gone, his reputation for governance spread far and wide.

sentences.zh: 江浙行省丞相別兒怯不花薦諸朝，升南陽知府，改建德路同知，俱未任。

translations.literal: The Jiang-Zhe Branch Secretariat chancellor Bayiqinbuqa recommended him to the court; he was promoted to prefect of Nanyang and to vice-intendant of Jiande Circuit, but took neither post.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Bayiqinbuqa of the Jiang-Zhe Branch Secretariat recommended him to court; he was promoted to prefect of Nanyang and vice-intendant of Jiande Circuit but assumed neither post.

sentences.zh: 至正八年，特旨遷為道州路總管，行至城外，撞賊已迫其後，相去僅二十里。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Zhizheng he was specially transferred by imperial order to circuit intendant of Daozhou; when he reached outside the city wall, bandit raiders had already pressed behind him, separated by only twenty li.
translations.idiomatic: In 1348 he was specially transferred by imperial order to circuit intendant of Daozhou; when he reached the outskirts, rebel forces were only twenty li behind him.

sentences.zh: 時湖南副使哈剌帖木兒屯兵城外，聞賊至，以乏軍需，欲退兵，興祖聞，即夜詣說留之。

translations.literal: At that time the Hunan vice commissioner Qaratemur encamped troops outside the city; hearing the bandits had come, because military supplies were lacking he wished to withdraw the army; Xingzu heard this and that night went to persuade him to stay.
translations.idiomatic: Hunan Vice Commissioner Qaratemur had troops encamped outside the walls; hearing the rebels approach, he meant to withdraw for lack of supplies, but Xingzu went to him that night and persuaded him to remain.

sentences.zh: 哈剌帖木兒曰：「明日得鈔五千錠、桐盾五百，乃可破賊。

translations.literal: Qaratemur said: "Tomorrow if I obtain five thousand ingots of paper money and five hundred paulownia shields, then I can break the bandits."
translations.idiomatic: Qaratemur said, "If I have five thousand ingots of paper money and five hundred paulownia shields by tomorrow, I can defeat the rebels."

sentences.zh: 」興祖許之。

translations.literal: " Xingzu promised him.
translations.idiomatic: " Xingzu promised to provide them.

sentences.zh: 明日甫入城視事，即以恩信勸諭鹽商，貸鈔五千錠，且取郡樓舊桐板為盾，日中皆備。

translations.literal: The next day, as soon as he entered the city to attend to affairs, he used kindness and trust to urge and instruct the salt merchants, borrowed five thousand ingots, and also took the old paulownia boards of the prefectural tower for shields; by midday all was ready.
translations.idiomatic: The next morning, as soon as he entered the city to take up his duties, he persuaded the salt merchants on trust to lend five thousand ingots and had old paulownia boards from the city tower fashioned into shields; by midday everything was ready.

sentences.zh: 哈剌帖木兒得鈔、盾，大喜，遂留，為御賊計。

translations.literal: Qaratemur obtained the notes and shields, was greatly pleased, and then stayed to plan defense against the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Qaratemur received the money and shields, was delighted, and stayed to plan the defense.

sentences.zh: 賊聞新總管至，一日具五百盾，以為大軍且至，中夕遁去。

translations.literal: The bandits heard the new intendant had arrived and in one day prepared five hundred shields; they thought a great army was about to come and at midnight fled.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels heard a new intendant had arrived and, seeing five hundred shields prepared in a single day, assumed a large army was coming and fled at midnight.

sentences.zh: 永明縣洞徭屢竊發為民害，興祖以手榜諭之。

translations.literal: In Yongming County the cave Yao repeatedly rose in theft and harmed the people; Xingzu used a hand-written notice to instruct them.
translations.idiomatic: Yao tribesmen in the caves of Yongming County had repeatedly raided the people; Xingzu addressed them with a personal proclamation.

sentences.zh: 皆曰：「林總管廉而愛民，不可犯也。

translations.literal: They all said: "Intendant Lin is incorrupt and loves the people; he cannot be violated."
translations.idiomatic: They all said, "Intendant Lin is honest and cares for the people; he must not be provoked."

sentences.zh: 」三年不入境。

translations.literal: " For three years they did not enter the border.
translations.idiomatic: " For three years they did not cross the border to raid.

sentences.zh: 春旱，蟲食麥苗，興祖為文禱之，大雨三日，蟲死而麥稔。

translations.literal: In spring there was drought; insects ate the wheat seedlings; Xingzu composed a text to pray; great rain fell three days; the insects died and the wheat ripened.
translations.idiomatic: When spring drought brought insects that devoured the wheat shoots, Xingzu wrote a prayer; rain fell heavily for three days, the pests died, and the wheat ripened.

sentences.zh: 已而罷興作，賑貧乏，輕徭薄斂，郡中大治，憲司考課，以道州為最。

translations.literal: Before long he stopped wasteful works, relieved the poor and needy, lightened corvée and reduced levies; the prefecture was greatly well governed; the surveillance commission's evaluation ranked Daozhou first.
translations.idiomatic: He then halted wasteful projects, relieved the poor, lightened corvée and taxes, and brought the circuit to good order; the surveillance commission ranked Daozhou highest in its review.

sentences.zh: 以年老致仕，終於家。

translations.literal: Because of old age he retired and ended his life at home.
translations.idiomatic: He retired on account of age and died at home.

sentences.zh: 觀音奴，字志能，唐兀人氏，居新州。

translations.literal: Guanyinnu, style name Zhineng, of the Tangut people, dwelt in Xin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Guanyinnu, whose courtesy name was Zhineng, was of Tangut descent and lived in Xin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 登泰定四年進士第。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the fourth year of Taiding.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in 1327.

sentences.zh: 由戶部主事，再轉而知歸德府。

translations.literal: From a clerk in the Ministry of Revenue he was twice transferred to know the affairs of Guide Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Starting as a clerk in the Ministry of Revenue, he was twice transferred until he became prefect of Guide.

sentences.zh: 廉明剛斷，發擿如神。

translations.literal: Incorrupt, clear, firm, and decisive, in exposing wrongdoing he was like a spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Incorrupt, discerning, and resolute, he uncovered hidden crimes as if by divine insight.

sentences.zh: 民有銜冤不直者，雖數十年前事，皆千里奔走來訴，觀音奴立為剖決，旬日悉清。

translations.literal: When the people bore grievances that had not been righted, even for matters of decades before they all ran a thousand li to sue; Guanyinnu immediately judged and decided for them, and within ten days all was cleared.
translations.idiomatic: If anyone nursed an old injustice, even from decades past, they would travel a thousand li to bring their case to him; Guanyinnu would hear them at once, and within ten days every backlog was cleared.

sentences.zh: 彰德富商任甲，抵睢陽，驢斃，令郄乙剖之，任以怒毆郄，經宿而死。

translations.literal: A wealthy merchant of Zhangde named Ren Jia reached Suiyang; his donkey died; he ordered Qie Yi to dissect it; Ren in anger beat Qie, and after one night Qie died.
translations.idiomatic: A rich Zhangde merchant named Ren Jia reached Suiyang; when his donkey died he ordered Qie Yi to butcher it, and in a rage Ren beat Qie to death overnight.

sentences.zh: 郄有妻王氏、妾孫氏，孫訴於官，官吏納任賄，謂郄非傷死，反抵孫罪，置之獄。

translations.literal: Qie had a wife, Lady Wang, and a concubine, Lady Sun; Sun sued at court; officials took Ren's bribes and said Qie had not died of wounds, instead charging Sun with a crime and putting her in prison.
translations.idiomatic: Qie left a wife, Lady Wang, and a concubine, Lady Sun; Sun brought suit, but officials took Ren's bribes, ruled the death was not from beating, and imprisoned Sun on a false charge.

sentences.zh: 王來訴冤，觀音奴立破械出孫於獄，呼府胥語之曰：「吾為文具香幣，若為吾以郄事禱諸城隍神，令神顯於吾。

translations.literal: Lady Wang came to sue for injustice; Guanyinnu immediately broke her shackles and released Sun from prison, called a prefectural clerk and told him: "I will prepare writing materials and incense and offerings; you shall pray for me to the City God concerning Qie's matter, and make the god reveal it to me."
translations.idiomatic: Lady Wang came to plead her case; Guanyinnu at once freed Sun from prison, summoned a prefectural clerk, and said, "Prepare incense and offerings—I want you to pray to the City God about Qie's death and bring the truth to light."

sentences.zh: 」有睢陽小吏，亦預郄事，畏觀音奴嚴明，且懼神顯其事，乃以任所賂鈔陳首曰：「郄實傷死，任賂上下匿其實，吾亦得賂，敢以首。

translations.literal: " There was a minor clerk of Suiyang who had also been involved in Qie's matter; fearing Guanyinnu's severity and also fearing the god would reveal the affair, he presented the notes Ren had bribed him with and confessed: "Qie truly died of wounds; Ren bribed superiors and subordinates to conceal the fact; I too received bribes and dare to confess."
translations.idiomatic: " A minor Suiyang clerk involved in the case, fearing Guanyinnu's rigor and divine exposure, confessed with the bribe notes in hand: "Qie died of the beating; Ren bought off officials to hide it, and I took bribes too—I confess."

sentences.zh: 」於是罪任商而釋孫妾。

translations.literal: " Thereupon Ren the merchant was punished and the concubine Sun was released.
translations.idiomatic: " Ren was punished and Lady Sun was released.

sentences.zh: 寧陵豪民楊甲，夙嗜王乙田三頃，不能得。

translations.literal: A powerful man of Ningling named Yang Jia had long coveted three qing of Wang Yi's land but could not obtain it.
translations.idiomatic: A Ningling magnate named Yang Jia had long coveted three qing of Wang Yi's fields but could never get them.

sentences.zh: 值王以飢攜其妻就食淮南，而王得疾死，其妻還，則田為楊據矣。

translations.literal: It happened that Wang, because of famine, took his wife to seek food in Huainan; Wang then fell ill and died, and when his wife returned, the land was already occupied by Yang.
translations.idiomatic: When famine struck, Wang took his wife to Huainan for food; Wang fell ill and died there, and by the time his wife returned, Yang had seized the fields.

sentences.zh: 王妻訴之官，楊行賄，偽作文憑，曰：「王在時已售我。

translations.literal: Wang's wife sued at court; Yang gave bribes and forged a written deed, saying: "While Wang was alive he had already sold to me.
translations.idiomatic: Wang's wife brought suit, but Yang bribed officials and forged a deed claiming, "Wang sold the land to me while he was still alive.

sentences.zh: 」觀音奴令王妻挽楊，同就崔府君神祠質之。

translations.literal: " Guanyinnu ordered Wang's wife to take Yang by the arm and together go to the shrine of Lord Cui to confront him there with an oath.
translations.idiomatic: " Guanyinnu had Wang's wife take Yang by the arm and go with him to the shrine of Lord Cui to settle the matter before the god.

sentences.zh: 楊懼神之靈，先期以羊酒浼巫囑神勿洩其事，及王與楊詣祠質之，果無所顯明。

translations.literal: Yang feared the god's power; beforehand he used sheep and wine to importune the shaman and bade the god not reveal the matter; when Wang and Yang went to the shrine to confront each other, indeed nothing was revealed.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing divine retribution, Yang had already bribed the shaman with sheep and wine to keep the god silent; when Wang and Yang went to the shrine, nothing was revealed.

sentences.zh: 觀音奴疑之，召巫詰問，巫吐其實曰：「楊以羊酒浼我囑神曰：'我實據王田，幸神勿洩也。

translations.literal: Guanyinnu became suspicious, summoned the shaman and questioned him, and the shaman told the truth: "Yang used sheep and wine to importune me and bade the god: 'I truly occupy Wang's land; may the god not reveal it.'
translations.idiomatic: Guanyinnu grew suspicious, summoned the shaman, and the shaman confessed: "Yang bribed me with sheep and wine and told the god, 'I really seized Wang's land—please don't expose me.'

sentences.zh: '」觀音奴因訊得其實，坐楊罪，歸其田王氏，責神而撤其祠。

translations.literal: '" Through inquiry Guanyinnu obtained the truth, punished Yang, returned the land to Lady Wang, blamed the god, and demolished the shrine.
translations.idiomatic: '" Guanyinnu got to the bottom of it, punished Yang, restored the fields to Lady Wang, and demolished the shrine in rebuke of the god.

sentences.zh: 亳州有蝗食民禾，觀音奴以事至亳，民以蝗訴，立取蝗向天祝之，以水研碎而飲，是歲蝗不為災。

translations.literal: At Bozhou locusts ate the people's grain; Guanyinnu came to Bozhou on business; the people complained about the locusts; he immediately took locusts, prayed to Heaven over them, ground them in water and drank it; that year the locusts did not become a disaster.
translations.idiomatic: When locusts devoured the crops at Bozhou, Guanyinnu happened to be there on business; the people appealed to him, and he at once took locusts, prayed heavenward, ground them in water, and drank the mixture—and that year the plague passed without harm.

sentences.zh: 後升為都水監官。

translations.literal: Later he was promoted to the office of Director of Waterworks.
translations.idiomatic: He was later promoted to Director of Waterworks.

sentences.zh: 周自強，字剛善，臨江路新喻州人。

translations.literal: Zhou Ziqiang, styled Gangshan, was a native of Xinyu Prefecture in Linjiang Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Ziqiang, styled Gangshan, was from Xinyu Prefecture in Linjiang Circuit.

sentences.zh: 好學能文，練於吏事，以文法推擇為吏。

translations.literal: He loved learning and was able in writing, practiced in clerical affairs, and through legal statutes was selected and chosen to serve as a clerk.
translations.idiomatic: He loved learning, wrote well, and was skilled in administrative work; selected by statute, he entered government service as a clerk.

sentences.zh: 泰定間，廣西洞徭反，自強往見徭酋，說以禍福，中其要害，徭酋立為罷兵，貢方物，納款請命。

translations.literal: During the Taiding era, cave Yao in Guangxi rebelled; Ziqiang went to see the Yao chieftain, explained fortune and misfortune, struck his vital point, and the chieftain immediately ceased warfare, presented tribute goods, and submitted in surrender to receive orders.
translations.idiomatic: During the Taiding reign, the cave Yao of Guangxi rose in revolt; Ziqiang went to their chieftain, argued the costs of war and peace, and hit the mark—the chieftain at once laid down arms, sent tribute, and sued for mercy.

sentences.zh: 事聞於朝，特旨超授廣西兩江道宣慰司都事。

translations.literal: When the affair reached the court, by special edict he was exceptionally promoted to Chief Secretary of the Guangxi Liangjiang Circuit Pacification Commission.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached court, an imperial directive bypassed the usual ranks and made him Chief Secretary of the Guangxi Liangjiang Pacification Commission.

sentences.zh: 轉饒州路經歷，遷婺州路義烏縣尹。

translations.literal: He transferred to be Supervisor of Raozhou Circuit, then was moved to Magistrate of Yiwu County in Wuzhou Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Supervisor of Raozhou Circuit, then was appointed magistrate of Yiwu County in Wuzhou Circuit.

sentences.zh: 周知民情，而性度寬厚，不為刻深。

translations.literal: He thoroughly understood the people's sentiments, and his nature was generous and broad, not harsh or severe.
translations.idiomatic: He knew the people well and was by nature generous rather than harsh.

sentences.zh: 民有以爭訟訴於庭者，一見即能知其曲直，然未遽加以刑責，必取經典中語，反覆開譬之，令其誦讀講解。

translations.literal: When people came to court with lawsuits from disputes, upon one meeting he could know right from wrong, yet he did not immediately impose punishment; he always took words from the classics, repeatedly opened and explained them, and made them recite, read, and discuss.
translations.idiomatic: When litigants came before him, he could tell right from wrong at a glance, yet he never rushed to punish; instead he drew passages from the classics, explained them again and again, and made the parties recite and discuss them.

sentences.zh: 若能悔悟首實，則原其罪；

translations.literal: If they could repent and confess the truth, then he pardoned their crimes;
translations.idiomatic: If they repented and confessed, he pardoned them;

sentences.zh: 若迷謬怙惡不悛，然後繩之以法不少貸。

translations.literal: if they were deluded and clung to evil without reform, then he bound them with the law and showed no leniency.
translations.idiomatic: if they persisted in wrongdoing, only then did he apply the law without mercy.

sentences.zh: 民畏且愛，獄訟頓息。

translations.literal: The people both feared and loved him, and litigation suddenly ceased.
translations.idiomatic: The people feared and loved him in equal measure, and lawsuits dwindled away.

sentences.zh: 民間田稅之籍多失實，以故差徭不平，自強出令履畝核之，民不能欺，文簿井井可考，於是賦役平均，貧富樂業。

translations.literal: Rural land-tax registers were often inaccurate, and for this reason labor corvée was uneven; Ziqiang issued an order to verify by foot-measurement across the fields, the people could not deceive him, the documents were orderly and examinable, and thus taxes and corvée were evened and rich and poor alike rejoiced in their occupations.
translations.idiomatic: Land-tax registers in the countryside were often wrong, skewing corvée assignments; Ziqiang ordered a field-by-field survey, and with no room to cheat, the records became reliable—taxes and labor duties were fair, and rich and poor alike could live in peace.

sentences.zh: 其聽訟決獄，物無遁情，黠吏欲以片言欺惑之不可得。

translations.literal: In hearing cases and deciding prisons, nothing escaped his knowledge; crafty clerks who wished to deceive him with a single phrase could not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: In court he missed nothing, and no clever clerk could mislead him with a word.

sentences.zh: 由是政治大行，聲譽籍甚。

translations.literal: From this his governance greatly prospered and his reputation resounded widely.
translations.idiomatic: His administration flourished, and his fame spread far and wide.

sentences.zh: 部使者數以廉能舉於朝，選授撫州路金溪縣尹，階奉議大夫，政績愈著。

translations.literal: Circuit inspectors repeatedly recommended him to the court for integrity and ability; he was selected and appointed Magistrate of Jinxi County in Fuzhou Circuit, rank Counselor-Director, and his achievements became even more outstanding.
translations.idiomatic: Inspectors repeatedly recommended him to court for integrity and competence; he was appointed magistrate of Jinxi County in Fuzhou Circuit with the rank of Counselor-Director, and his record grew still brighter.

sentences.zh: 以亞中大夫、江州路總管致仕。

translations.literal: He retired as Circuit Intendant of Jiangzhou Circuit with the rank of Sub-Counselor of the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He retired as intendant of Jiangzhou Circuit with the rank of Sub-Counselor of the Palace.

sentences.zh: 白景亮，字明甫，南陽人。

translations.literal: Bai Jingliang, styled Mingfu, was a native of Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Bai Jingliang, styled Mingfu, was from Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 明法律，善書算。

translations.literal: He understood law and was skilled in writing and calculation.
translations.idiomatic: He knew the law and was adept at writing and arithmetic.

sentences.zh: 由征東行省譯史有勞，超遷南恩知州，升沔陽府尹，奏最於朝，特授衢州路總管。

translations.literal: For meritorious service as translator-clerk in the Eastern Expedition Branch Secretariat, he was exceptionally promoted to Prefect of Nan'en, then raised to Prefect of Mianyang Prefecture; when he reported top performance at court, he was specially appointed Circuit Intendant of Quzhou Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: For distinguished service as a translator-clerk in the Eastern Expedition Branch Secretariat, he was promoted to prefect of Nan'en, then to prefect of Mianyang; after reporting the year's best results at court, he was specially appointed intendant of Quzhou Circuit.

sentences.zh: 先是，為郡者於民間徭役，不盡校​​田畝以為則，吏得併緣高下其手，富民或優有餘力，而貧弱不能勝者，多至破產失業。

translations.literal: Previously, those who governed the prefecture in levying local corvée did not fully verify field acreage as the standard; clerks could manipulate it up and down at will; wealthy households sometimes had surplus labor, but the poor and weak who could not bear it often went bankrupt and lost their livelihoods.
translations.idiomatic: Before his time, prefectural corvée was not tied rigorously to acreage; clerks manipulated the rolls at will, and while the wealthy often had labor to spare, the poor were driven to ruin.

sentences.zh: 景亮深知其弊，乃始核驗田畝以均之，役之輕重，一視田之多寡，大小家各使得宜，咸便安之，由是民不勞而事易集，他郡邑皆取以為法。

translations.literal: Jingliang deeply understood this abuse; he then began to verify and check field acreage to equalize it; the weight of corvée was entirely determined by the amount of land; large and small households each obtained what was fitting, all found it convenient and settled; from this the people were not overworked yet tasks were easily accomplished, and other prefectures and counties all took it as a model.
translations.idiomatic: Jingliang saw the abuse clearly and began verifying acreage so corvée matched landholding; large and small households alike found the burden fair, work got done without crushing the people, and other jurisdictions copied his method.

sentences.zh: 郡學之政久弛，從祀諸賢無塑像，諸生無廩膳，祭服樂器有缺，景亮皆為備之，儒風大振，縉紳稱頌焉。

translations.literal: Prefectural school administration had long been lax; accompanying worthies in sacrifice had no statues, students had no grain rations, sacrificial robes and musical instruments were lacking—Jingliang provided for all of these; Confucian influence greatly revived, and gentry officials praised him.
translations.idiomatic: The prefectural school had long been neglected—honored sages had no statues, students no stipends, ritual robes and instruments were missing; Jingliang supplied them all, Confucian learning revived, and the gentry sang his praises.

sentences.zh: 景亮性廉介勤苦，自奉甚薄，妻尤儉約，惟以脫粟對飯而已。

translations.literal: Jingliang's nature was integrity and austerity with diligent hardship; his personal upkeep was very spare; his wife was especially frugal—they had only unhusked grain with their rice.
translations.idiomatic: Jingliang was incorruptible and frugal, living on very little; his wife was even more sparing—they ate nothing but unpolished grain with their rice.

sentences.zh: 部使者嘗上其事，特詔褒美，賜以宮錦，改授台州路總管。

translations.literal: A circuit inspector once reported this to the court; by special edict he was commended, granted palace brocade, and reassigned as Circuit Intendant of Taizhou Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: When an inspector reported this to court, an imperial edict commended him, granted palace brocade, and transferred him to intendant of Taizhou Circuit.

sentences.zh: 卒於官。

translations.literal: He died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office.

sentences.zh: 王艮，字止善，紹興諸暨人。

translations.literal: Wang Gen, styled Zhishan, was a native of Zhuji in Shaoxing.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Gen, styled Zhishan, was from Zhuji in Shaoxing.

sentences.zh: 尚氣節，讀書務明理以致用，不苟事言說。

translations.literal: He valued integrity and principle; in reading he sought to clarify principle for practical use, and did not casually engage in empty talk.
translations.idiomatic: He prized integrity, read to grasp principle and put it to use, and disdained idle talk.

sentences.zh: 淮東廉訪司辟為書吏，遷淮西。

translations.literal: The Huaidong Surveillance Commission recruited him as a clerk and he was transferred to Huaixi.
translations.idiomatic: The Huaidong Surveillance Commission recruited him as a clerk, and he was later transferred to Huaixi.

sentences.zh: 會例革南士，就為吏於兩淮都轉運鹽使司，以歲月及格，授廬州錄事判官。

translations.literal: When regulations abolished southern scholars, he served as a clerk in the Lianghuai Salt Transport Commission; when his years of service reached qualification, he was appointed Assistant Magistrate of Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When a regulation barred southern degree-holders, he became a clerk in the Lianghuai Salt Transport Commission; after his years of service qualified, he was appointed assistant magistrate of Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 淮東宣慰司辟為令史，以廉能稱。

translations.literal: The Huaidong Pacification Commission recruited him as a chief clerk, and he was praised for integrity and ability.
translations.idiomatic: The Huaidong Pacification Commission recruited him as chief clerk, and he won a reputation for integrity and competence.

sentences.zh: 再調峽州總管府知事，又辟江浙行省掾史。

translations.literal: He was transferred again to Clerk of the Xiangzhou Circuit Intendant's office, then recruited as a clerk of the Jiangzhe Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to clerk of the Xiangzhou intendant's office, then recruited as a clerk of the Jiangzhe Branch Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 會朝廷復立諸市舶司，艮從省官至泉州，建言：「若買舊有之船以付舶商，則費省而工易集，且可絕官吏侵欺掊克之弊。

translations.literal: When the court re-established the maritime trade offices, Gen followed the provincial officials to Quanzhou and offered a proposal: "If one buys existing ships to entrust to merchant voyagers, expense is saved and labor is easily assembled, and one can also cut off the abuse of officials' encroachment, fraud, and extortion.
translations.idiomatic: When the court restored the maritime trade offices, Gen accompanied the provincial officials to Quanzhou and proposed: "If the government buys existing vessels and assigns them to merchant fleets, costs fall, work proceeds quickly, and officials can no longer skim and squeeze.

sentences.zh: 」中書省報如艮言。

translations.literal: " The Central Secretariat replied as Gen had said.
translations.idiomatic: " The Central Secretariat approved Gen's proposal.

sentences.zh: 凡為船六宗，省官錢五十餘萬緡。

translations.literal: In all six large ships were built, saving more than five hundred thousand strings of official money.
translations.idiomatic: Six large ships were built in all, saving more than five hundred thousand strings of official funds.

sentences.zh: 歷建德縣尹，除兩浙都轉運鹽使司經歷。

translations.literal: He served as Magistrate of Jiande County, then was appointed Supervisor of the Liangzhe Salt Transport Commission.
translations.idiomatic: He served as magistrate of Jiande County, then was appointed supervisor of the Liangzhe Salt Transport Commission.

sentences.zh: 紹興路總管王克敬，以計口食鹽不便，嘗言於，行省，未報，而克敬為轉運使，集議欲稍損其額，以紓民力。

translations.literal: Shaoxing Circuit Intendant Wang Kejing, finding per-capita salt tax inconvenient, had once petitioned the Branch Secretariat but received no reply; when Kejing became Salt Commissioner, he convened a meeting intending to slightly reduce the quota to relieve the people's burden.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Kejing, intendant of Shaoxing Circuit, had found the per-capita salt levy burdensome and once petitioned the Branch Secretariat without reply; when he became salt commissioner, he convened a meeting to trim the quota and ease the people's load.

sentences.zh: 沮之者以為有成籍不可改，艮毅然曰：「民實寡而強賦多民之錢，今死、徙已眾矣，顧重改成籍而輕棄民命乎！

translations.literal: Dissenters said established registers could not be changed; Gen resolutely said: "The people are truly few yet we forcibly levy much of their money; already many have died or fled—would we rather cling to altering the register than lightly abandon the people's lives!
translations.idiomatic: Opponents argued the established register could not be changed; Gen declared firmly: "The people are dwindling while we force heavy levies on them—many have already died or fled! Would we rather preserve the register than save their lives!

sentences.zh: 且浙右之郡，商賈輻輳，未嘗以口計也。

translations.literal: Moreover the prefectures of western Zhejiang are thronged with merchants and have never been assessed by head count.
translations.idiomatic: Besides, the prefectures of western Zhejiang teem with merchants and were never meant to be taxed by head count.

sentences.zh: 移其所賦，散於商旅之所聚，實為良法。

translations.literal: Shifting the levy and spreading it where travelers and merchants gather is truly a good method.
translations.idiomatic: Shifting the levy to where travelers and merchants congregate is truly the better policy.

sentences.zh: 」於是議歲減紹興食鹽五千六百引。

translations.literal: " Thereupon it was agreed to reduce Shaoxing's salt quota by five thousand six hundred yin per year.
translations.idiomatic: " The assembly agreed to cut Shaoxing's annual salt quota by five thousand six hundred yin.

sentences.zh: 尋有復排前議者，艮欲辭職去，丞相聞之，亟遣留艮，而議遂定。

translations.literal: Soon some revived the previous proposal; Gen wanted to resign and leave; the chancellor heard of it, urgently sent to retain Gen, and the decision was settled.
translations.idiomatic: When opponents later revived the old plan, Gen threatened to resign; the chancellor heard and urgently ordered him to stay, and the reform held.

sentences.zh: 遷海道漕運都萬戶府經歷。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Supervisor of the Maritime Grain Transport Office of Myriad Households.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to supervisor of the Maritime Grain Transport Office.

sentences.zh: 紹興之官糧入海運者十萬石，城距海十八里，歲令有司拘民船以備短送，吏胥得併緣以虐民。

translations.literal: Shaoxing's official grain entering maritime transport was one hundred thousand shi; the city was eighteen li from the sea; each year officials were ordered to requisition civilian boats for short hauls; clerks could manipulate this to abuse the people.
translations.idiomatic: Shaoxing shipped one hundred thousand shi of tribute grain by sea; the city stood eighteen li inland, and each year officials requisitioned civilian boats for the short haul—giving clerks room to torment the people.

sentences.zh: 及至海次，主運者又不即受，有折缺之患。

translations.literal: When they reached the seacoast, transport overseers did not immediately receive it, and there was loss from shortage.
translations.idiomatic: At the coast the transport officers delayed acceptance, inviting shortages and losses.

sentences.zh: 艮執言曰：「運戶既有官賦之直，何復為是紛紛也！

translations.literal: Gen insisted: "Transport households already receive official payment for grain—why all this turmoil!
translations.idiomatic: Gen protested: "Transport households already receive official payment—why all this needless trouble!

sentences.zh: 」乃責運戶自載糧入運船。

translations.literal: " He then required transport households to load their own grain into transport ships.
translations.idiomatic: " He ordered transport households to load their own grain directly onto the transport ships.

sentences.zh: 運船為風所敗者，當核實除其數，移文往返，連數歲不絕，艮取吏牘披閱，即除其糧五萬二千八百石、鈔二百五十萬緡，運戶乃免於破家。

translations.literal: For transport ships wrecked by wind, the shortfall should be verified and deducted; documents shuttled back and forth for years without end; Gen took the clerical records and reviewed them, immediately deducting fifty-two thousand eight hundred shi of grain and two million five hundred thousand strings of notes—transport households were thus spared bankruptcy.
translations.idiomatic: Grain lost when ships were wrecked in storms should be verified and written off, yet documents shuttled back and forth for years; Gen reviewed the files and at once cancelled fifty-two thousand eight hundred shi of grain and two million five hundred thousand strings of notes, saving transport households from ruin.

sentences.zh: 遷江浙行省檢校官。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Inspecting Secretary of the Jiangzhe Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to inspecting secretary of the Jiangzhe Branch Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 有詣中書訴松江富民包隱田土，為糧一百七十餘萬石；

translations.literal: Someone petitioned the Central Secretariat accusing wealthy men of Songjiang of concealing land, totaling more than 1.7 million shi of grain tax;
translations.idiomatic: Someone petitioned the Central Secretariat claiming Songjiang's wealthy had concealed land worth more than 1.7 million shi of grain tax;

sentences.zh: 沙盪，為鈔五百餘萬緡；

translations.literal: sand flats, more than five million strings of notes;
translations.idiomatic: and sand flats worth more than five million strings of notes;

sentences.zh: 宜立官府糾察收追之。

translations.literal: officials should be established to investigate and recover it.
translations.idiomatic: and urged that new offices be created to investigate and recover the revenue.

sentences.zh: 中書移行省議，遣官驗視，而鬆江獨當十九。

translations.literal: The Central Secretariat referred it to the Branch Secretariat for discussion and sent officials to inspect; Songjiang alone would bear nine-tenths.
translations.idiomatic: The Central Secretariat referred the matter to the Branch Secretariat and sent officials to inspect; Songjiang alone would bear nine-tenths of the burden.

sentences.zh: 艮至松江，條陳曲折，以破其誑妄，言其「不過欲竦朝廷之聽而報宿怨，且冀創立衙門，為徼名爵計耳。

translations.literal: Gen reached Songjiang, laid out the details point by point, and refuted the fraud, saying: "This is merely to startle the court's ears and settle old grudges, and to hope to create new offices for the sake of seeking fame and rank.
translations.idiomatic: Gen went to Songjiang, laid out the case in detail, and exposed the fraud, declaring: "This is nothing but an attempt to alarm the court, settle old scores, and win new offices for the sake of fame.

sentences.zh: 萬一民心動搖，患生不測，豈國家培養根本之策哉！

translations.literal: If by any chance popular sentiment is shaken and unforeseen calamity arises, is this a policy for the state to nurture its foundation!
translations.idiomatic: If popular sentiment is shaken and unforeseen trouble follows, how is that a policy for nurturing the state's foundation!

sentences.zh: 」艮言上，事遂寢。

translations.literal: " When Gen's words reached the court, the matter was dropped.
translations.idiomatic: " When his report reached the court, the proposal was shelved.

sentences.zh: 除江西行省左右司員外郎。

translations.literal: He was appointed Assistant Director of the Left and Right Offices of the Jiangxi Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed assistant director in the Left and Right Offices of the Jiangxi Branch Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 吉之安福有小吏，誣民欺隱詭寄田租​​九千餘石，初止八家，前後數十年，株連至千家，行省數遣官按問，吏已伏其虛誑，而有司喜功生事者，复勒其民報合徵糧六百餘石，憲司援詔條革去，終莫能止。

translations.literal: In Anfu of Ji there was a minor clerk who falsely accused the people of concealing and fraudulently registering land rent of more than nine thousand shi; at first only eight households were involved, but over decades the case implicated a thousand; the Branch Secretariat repeatedly sent officials to investigate; the clerk had already confessed to the falsehood, yet officials eager for achievement stirred up trouble again and forced the people to report a combined levy of more than six hundred shi of grain; the surveillance commission cited an edict to abolish it, yet in the end could not stop it.
translations.idiomatic: At Anfu in Ji, a petty clerk falsely accused locals of concealing more than nine thousand shi of land tax; what began with eight households spread over decades to a thousand; though the clerk confessed to fraud and the surveillance commission cited an edict to cancel the levy, ambitious officials kept pressing for six hundred more shi, and nothing could stop them.

sentences.zh: 艮到官，首言：「是州之糧，比元經理已增一千一百餘石，豈復有欺隱詭寄者乎？

translations.literal: When Gen took office, he first said: "This prefecture's grain quota, compared with the Yuan initial survey, has already increased by more than eleven hundred shi—how could there still be concealment and fraudulent registration?
translations.idiomatic: On taking office Gen said at once: "This prefecture's grain quota already exceeds the Yuan baseline by more than eleven hundred shi—how could concealment still be possible?

sentences.zh: 準憲司所擬可也。

translations.literal: The surveillance commission's proposal may be approved.
translations.idiomatic: The surveillance commission's proposal should stand.

sentences.zh: 」行省用艮言，悉蠲之。

translations.literal: " The Branch Secretariat adopted Gen's words and remitted it all.
translations.idiomatic: " The Branch Secretariat followed Gen's advice and remitted the entire levy.

sentences.zh: 艮在任歲餘，以中憲大夫、淮東道宣慰副使致仕。

translations.literal: Gen served a little over a year, then retired as Vice Commissioner of the Huaidong Circuit Pacification Commission with the rank of Regular Counselor.
translations.idiomatic: After little more than a year in office, he retired as vice commissioner of the Huaidong Pacification Commission with the rank of Regular Counselor.

sentences.zh: 卒年七十一。

translations.literal: He died at the age of seventy-one.
translations.idiomatic: He died at seventy-one.

sentences.zh: 盧琦，字希韓，惠安人，登至正二年進士第。

translations.literal: Lu Qi, styled Xihan, was a native of Huian; he passed the jinshi examination in the second year of Zhizheng.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Qi, styled Xihan, was from Huian and passed the jinshi examination in the second year of Zhizheng.

sentences.zh: 十二年，稍遷至永春縣尹。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he was gradually promoted to Magistrate of Yongchun County.
translations.idiomatic: By the twelfth year he had risen to magistrate of Yongchun County.

sentences.zh: 始至，賑饑饉，止橫斂，均賦役，減口鹽一百餘引，蠲包銀榷鐵之無徵者。

translations.literal: When he first arrived, he relieved famine, stopped arbitrary exactions, equalized taxes and corvée, reduced the per-capita salt levy by more than one hundred yin, and remitted uncollected package-silver and iron monopoly dues.
translations.idiomatic: On arrival he relieved famine, halted illegal levies, equalized taxes and corvée, cut the per-capita salt quota by more than one hundred yin, and cancelled uncollected package-silver and iron monopoly dues.

sentences.zh: 已而訟息民安，乃新學宮，延師儒課子弟，月書季考，文風翕然。

translations.literal: Before long litigation ceased and the people were at peace; he then rebuilt the school, invited Confucian teachers to instruct the young, held monthly compositions and quarterly examinations, and literary culture flourished together.
translations.idiomatic: Soon lawsuits faded and the people settled; he rebuilt the school, hired teachers for the youth, held monthly essays and quarterly exams, and learning flourished.

sentences.zh: 鄰邑仙遊盜發，琦適在邑境，盜遙見之，迎拜曰：「此永春大夫也。

translations.literal: Bandits rose in neighboring Xianyou County; Qi happened to be within his county's borders; the bandits saw him from afar, came forward and bowed, saying: "This is the grandee of Yongchun.
translations.idiomatic: When bandits broke out in neighboring Xianyou, Qi happened to be on the border; seeing him from afar, they came forward and bowed, saying, "This is the magistrate of Yongchun.

sentences.zh: 為大夫百姓者，何幸之大乎！

translations.literal: To be the people of such a grandee—what great fortune!
translations.idiomatic: What fortune to be governed by such a magistrate!

sentences.zh: 吾邑長乃以暴毒驅我，故至此耳。

translations.literal: Our county chief drove us here with cruelty and violence—that is all.
translations.idiomatic: Our own magistrate drove us out with cruelty—that is why we are here.

sentences.zh: 」琦因立馬喻以禍福，眾皆投刃槊，請縛其酋以自新，琦許之。

translations.literal: " Qi thereupon halted his horse and explained fortune and misfortune; all cast aside blades and spears, asked to bind their chieftain to reform themselves, and Qi consented.
translations.idiomatic: " Qi reined in his horse and reasoned with them about the consequences; they threw down their weapons, asked to bind their leader and submit, and Qi agreed.

sentences.zh: 酋至，琦械送帥府，自是威惠行於境外。

translations.literal: When the chieftain arrived, Qi sent him in fetters to the marshal's headquarters; from then on his authority and kindness extended beyond the border.
translations.idiomatic: When the chieftain was brought in, Qi sent him in chains to the regional command; from then on his authority and benevolence reached beyond the county line.

sentences.zh: 十三年，泉郡大饑，死者相枕籍。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, Quan Prefecture suffered great famine; the dead lay piled head to foot.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year a great famine struck Quan Prefecture, and the dead lay stacked upon one another.

sentences.zh: 其能行者，皆老幼扶攜，就食永春。

translations.literal: Those who could walk, old and young supporting one another, came to Yongchun to seek food.
translations.idiomatic: Those who could still walk—old and young helping one another—streamed into Yongchun for food.

sentences.zh: 琦命分諸浮屠及大家使食之，所存活不可勝計。

translations.literal: Qi ordered distribution among the Buddhist monasteries and great households to feed them; those who survived were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Qi arranged for monasteries and wealthy households to feed them, saving countless lives.

sentences.zh: 十四年，安溪寇數万人來襲永春。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, bandits from Anxi numbering tens of thousands came to attack Yongchun.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year tens of thousands of bandits from Anxi attacked Yongchun.

sentences.zh: 琦聞，召邑民喻之曰：「汝等能戰則與之戰，不能，則我當獨死之爾。

translations.literal: When Qi heard, he summoned the county people and told them: "If you can fight, then fight them; if not, then I alone shall die for you.
translations.idiomatic: When he heard, Qi summoned the people and said: "If you can fight, fight; if not, I alone will die here.

sentences.zh: 」眾皆感憤，曰：「使君何言也！

translations.literal: " All were moved and indignant, saying: "Magistrate, why speak thus!
translations.idiomatic: " The crowd was stirred and cried: "My lord, how can you say such a thing!

sentences.zh: 使君父母，我民赤子，其忍以父母畀賊邪！

translations.literal: The magistrate is parent to us, the people are his infants—how could we bear to hand our parents over to bandits!
translations.idiomatic: You are our parent and we your children—would we hand our parent over to bandits!

sentences.zh: 且彼寇方將虜掠我妻子，焚毀我室廬，乃一邑深仇也。

translations.literal: Moreover those bandits are about to seize and plunder our wives and children and burn our houses—this is a deep enmity for the whole county.
translations.idiomatic: Besides, they come to seize our wives and children and burn our homes—this is a blood feud for the whole county.

sentences.zh: 今日之事，有進無退，使君其勿以為憂。

translations.literal: Today's affair allows advance, not retreat; magistrate, please do not worry.
translations.idiomatic: Today we advance, not retreat—my lord, do not worry.

sentences.zh: 」因踴躍爭奮。

translations.literal: " Thereupon they leaped forward, vying to be first.
translations.idiomatic: " They surged forward, eager to fight.

sentences.zh: 琦率以攻賊，大破之。

translations.literal: Qi led them to attack the bandits and routed them utterly.
translations.idiomatic: Qi led them against the bandits and won a great victory.

sentences.zh: 明日，賊复傾巢而至，又破之。

translations.literal: The next day the bandits came again with their full force, and he defeated them again.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the bandits returned in full force, and he defeated them again.

sentences.zh: 大小三十餘戰，斬獲一千二百餘人，而邑民無死傷者。

translations.literal: In more than thirty battles large and small, more than twelve hundred were killed or captured, yet among the county people there were none dead or wounded.
translations.idiomatic: In more than thirty engagements they killed or captured over twelve hundred enemies, yet not one townsman was killed or wounded.

sentences.zh: 賊大衄，遂遁去。

translations.literal: The bandits suffered a great defeat and thereupon fled away.
translations.idiomatic: Badly beaten, the bandits fled.

sentences.zh: 時兵革四起，列郡皆洶洶不寧，獨永春晏然，無異承平時。

translations.literal: At that time warfare rose on every side and every prefecture was turbulent and unsettled; Yongchun alone was tranquil, no different from times of peace.
translations.idiomatic: While war erupted everywhere and neighboring prefectures trembled, Yongchun alone remained calm, as peaceful as in better days.

sentences.zh: 十六年，改調寧德縣尹而去。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he was transferred to be magistrate of Ningde County and left.
translations.idiomatic: In 1356 he was reassigned as magistrate of Ningde County and departed.

sentences.zh: 鄒伯顏，字從吉，高唐人。

translations.literal: Zou Boyan, style name Congji, was a man of Gaotang.
translations.idiomatic: Zou Boyan, whose courtesy name was Congji, came from Gaotang.

sentences.zh: 為建寧崇安縣尹。

translations.literal: He served as magistrate of Chong'an County in Jianning.
translations.idiomatic: He served as magistrate of Chong'an County in Jianning.

sentences.zh: 崇安之為邑，區別其土田，名之曰都者五十，五十都之田上送官者，為糧六千石。

translations.literal: As a county Chong'an divided its fields and soil; those named du numbered fifty; the fields of the fifty du presented upward to the government amounted to six thousand shi of grain.
translations.idiomatic: Chong'an divided its land into fifty districts called du, whose combined tax yield to the government was six thousand shi of grain.

sentences.zh: 其大家以五十餘家，而兼五千石；

translations.literal: The great households, more than fifty families, together bore five thousand shi;
translations.idiomatic: More than fifty wealthy households shouldered five thousand shi among them;

sentences.zh: 細民以四百餘家，而合一千石。

translations.literal: the lesser people, more than four hundred families, together made one thousand shi.
translations.idiomatic: while more than four hundred poor households together owed only one thousand shi.

sentences.zh: 大家之田，連跨數都，而細民之糧，或僅升合。

translations.literal: The great households' fields stretched across several du, while the lesser people's grain tax might be only a sheng or he.
translations.idiomatic: The rich held fields spanning several districts, while some poor households owed only a few pints of grain.

sentences.zh: 有司常以四百之細民，配五十大家之役，故貧者受役旬日，而家已破。

translations.literal: Officials constantly matched the four hundred lesser people to the corvée of the fifty great households; therefore the poor, after ten days of corvée, already had ruined families.
translations.idiomatic: Officials routinely assigned the four hundred poor households to serve the corvée obligations of the fifty rich ones, so a peasant's family could be ruined within ten days of forced labor.

sentences.zh: 伯顏曰：「貧弱之受困，一至此乎！

translations.literal: Boyan said: "That the poor and weak should suffer distress to this degree!"
translations.idiomatic: Boyan exclaimed, "Must the poor and weak be driven to such straits!"

sentences.zh: 」乃取其糧籍而分計從，有糧一石者，受一石之役，有糧升斗者，受升斗之役。

translations.literal: " He then took their grain registers and divided and reckoned corvée accordingly: whoever had one shi of grain bore one shi's corvée; whoever had sheng or dou bore sheng or dou's corvée.
translations.idiomatic: " He took the tax registers and apportioned corvée by actual yield: one shi of grain meant one shi of labor, a few pints meant a few pints of labor.

sentences.zh: 田多者受數都之役而不可辭，田少者稱其所出而無倖免。

translations.literal: Those with much land bore corvée across several du and could not decline; those with little land reported what they produced and had no lucky escape.
translations.idiomatic: Large landowners bore corvée across several districts and could not refuse; smallholders paid in proportion to their output and could not evade.

sentences.zh: 貧因無告之民，始得以休息。

translations.literal: The poor, helpless people were then able to rest.
translations.idiomatic: The poorest people, who had nowhere to turn, were finally able to breathe.

sentences.zh: 崇安賦役之均，遂為四方最。

translations.literal: Chong'an's evenness in levies and corvée thus became foremost in the four quarters.
translations.idiomatic: Chong'an's fair apportionment of taxes and corvée became the best in the realm.

sentences.zh: 邑有宋趙抃所鑿溝，溉民田數千畝。

translations.literal: The county had a ditch dug by Zhao Bian of Song, irrigating several thousand mu of the people's fields.
translations.idiomatic: The county had an irrigation ditch dug in Song times by Zhao Bian, watering several thousand mu of farmland.

sentences.zh: 歲久，溝湮而田廢。

translations.literal: Years passed; the ditch silted up and the fields were abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: Over the years the ditch silted up and the fields lay fallow.

sentences.zh: 伯顏修長溝十里，繞楓樹陂，累石以為固，溝悉复抃遺跡，而田為常稔，民賴其利。

translations.literal: Boyan repaired a long ditch ten li, winding around Maple Tree Embankment, piling stones to make it firm; the ditch fully restored Bian's traces, and the fields became regularly ripe; the people relied on its benefit.
translations.idiomatic: Boyan rebuilt ten li of channel around Maple Tree Embankment, reinforced it with stone, fully restored Zhao Bian's work, and brought the fields back to steady harvest—the people prospered from it.

sentences.zh: 安慶路嘗得造偽鈔者，遣卒械其囚至崇安，求其黨而執之，囚與卒結謀，望風入良民家肆虐。

translations.literal: Anqing Circuit once captured counterfeiters of notes; they sent soldiers with the prisoner in fetters to Chong'an to seek his gang and seize them; the prisoner and soldiers plotted together and, seeing their chance, entered good commoners' homes and rampaged.
translations.idiomatic: Anqing Circuit once caught counterfeiters and sent soldiers escorting a prisoner to Chong'an to round up accomplices; the prisoner and guards conspired to raid innocent households at will.

sentences.zh: 伯顏捕訊得其狀，即執而歸諸安慶，自是偽造之連逮無濫及崇安者。

translations.literal: Boyan captured and interrogated them and obtained the facts; he immediately seized them and returned them to Anqing; from this the implicated parties in counterfeiting did not overflow to harm Chong'an.
translations.idiomatic: Boyan investigated, arrested them, and sent them back to Anqing, so Chong'an was no longer swept up in the counterfeiting dragnet.

sentences.zh: 於是行省帥府、御史憲府咸舉其能。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Branch Secretariat, marshal's headquarters, and surveillance commission all recommended his ability.
translations.idiomatic: The Branch Secretariat, the marshal's office, and the surveillance commission all commended his competence.

sentences.zh: 選調漳州路判官。

translations.literal: He was selected and transferred to assistant prefect of Zhangzhou Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was selected for transfer as assistant prefect of Zhangzhou Circuit.

sentences.zh: 劉秉直，字清臣，大都武清人。

translations.literal: Liu Bingzhi, style name Qingchen, was a man of Wuqing in the Great Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bingzhi, whose courtesy name was Qingchen, came from Wuqing near the capital.

sentences.zh: 至正八年，來為衛輝路總管​​，平徭役，興教化，敦四民之業，崇五土之利，養鰥寡，恤孤獨。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Zhizheng he came to be circuit intendant of Weihui; he equalized corvée, revived teaching and transformation, encouraged the occupations of the four classes of people, honored the profits of the five soils, nourished widows and widowers, and pitied the orphaned and alone.
translations.idiomatic: In 1348 he became circuit intendant of Weihui, equalized corvée, promoted education, encouraged all trades and agriculture, cared for widows and orphans, and relieved the destitute.

sentences.zh: 賊劫汲縣民張聚鈔一千二百錠而殺之，賊不獲，秉直具詞致禱城隍祠，而使人伺於死所，忽有村民阿蓮者，戰怖僕地，具言賊之姓名及所在，乃命尉襲之，果得賊於汴，遂正其罪。
